privacy_redaction.hardware_identity: Public copy: physical GPU model and UUID are withheld; architecture labels do not identify a particular supported profile.
privacy_redaction.provenance: Measurements are retained. Embedded signatures, source digests and byte counts describe the private original records unless explicitly labeled as public-copy digests.
privacy_redaction.usage: Redacted review material, not an unmodified calibration input or a hardware identity attestation.

limitations: Synthetic fixed-length text and single-GPU Hugging Face Trainer only.
Each method has 6 independent process runs; measured updates within a process are not independent process observations.
The holdout validates step-time and peak-memory extrapolation, not a complete multi-epoch target run.
Total training-loop estimates exclude model initialization, tokenization, evaluation and checkpoint I/O.
Allocator peaks exclude driver context and other non-PyTorch GPU allocations.
Successful collection is not an accuracy certification or model-quality assessment.
Uncalibrated analytical errors are retained alongside calibrated comparisons.
Calibration and holdouts use the same shape; longer sequences, larger models and other frameworks need their own evidence.
methodology: Each method uses 6 independent CUDA processes: one calibration with 2 warmup + 4 measured updates, and 5 holdouts with 2 warmup + 20 measured updates each; every process uses a different seed. No concurrent FakeGPU test suite during the recorded run.

limitations: Synthetic text measures fixed-shape training, not convergence or arbitrary input pipelines.
Timing excludes model initialization, checkpoint saving, and evaluation.
Checkpoint identity streams the selected weight files before model loading; its measured read cost is excluded from training-loop time.
Timing samples are complete optimizer updates divided by gradient accumulation.
Peak allocated/reserved memory is PyTorch allocator memory, not total device usage.
This probe runs Hugging Face Trainer and cannot validate another framework's execution.
